title: Measuring Claim‑to‑Action Rates and Automated Defenses in Simulated Agentic NetOps Pipelines
abstract: We preregistered and executed a paired confirmatory study (hosted-netops-gvr-v1-2026-08-26) that measures how often LLM‑produced NetOps configuration proposals would produce unsafe simulated deployments (the claim→action or unsafe‑execution rate) and whether an automated guarded pipeline reduces that rate. We generated 300 intent→configuration tasks and ran paired baseline and guarded conditions; 272 complete pairs were analyzable. On those 272 pairs the executed guarded pipeline (validator + simulated human‑gate on a shared initial generation; see Disclosure) yielded baseline safe = 271/272 and guarded safe = 272/272, an absolute paired increase = 0.003676470588235281 (95% bootstrap percentile CI [0.0000, 0.011029411764705883]; exact McNemar two‑sided p = 1.0). Conservatively including 28 both‑failed pairs as unsafe (preregistered "failure_as_unsafe" sensitivity) gives guarded − baseline = 0.0033333333 on N=300. A documented, artifact‑backed deviation occurred: the preregistered multimodel consensus ensemble was not executed (execution manifest stage_counts: {"shared_initial_generation": 300, "repair": 1}); the executed guarded condition therefore functioned as the deterministic validator + simulated human‑gate applied to a shared initial generation. All execution, scoring, and validator artifacts and SHA‑256 hashes are archived and cited in the Disclosure Statement. We report results exactly as observed, document the preregistration vs execution deviation, and discuss construct, internal, and external validity.

sections.introduction: Agentic NetOps pipelines convert high‑level intent into configuration changes that may be executed automatically; a central operational hazard is the claim→action gap, where fluent LLM assertions become state changes with operational consequence. Motivated by prior work on verifier‑assisted and generate–validate–repair architectures and by operational threat pipelines that measure text→action risks, we preregistered (hosted-netops-gvr-v1-2026-08-26) a paired evaluation to (i) estimate the claim→action (unsafe‑execution) rate in a simulated NetOps environment and (ii) test whether a guarded pipeline reduces that rate relative to an unguarded baseline. Research question: In an isolated NetOps simulator, what is the absolute paired difference in safe outcome rates between a baseline (single generation → validator → execute) and a guarded pipeline (preregistered: validator + 3‑model consensus + simulated human‑gate)? Contributions: 1) a preregistered, artifact‑backed paired measurement with full execution and scoring provenance; 2) concrete, artifact‑documented reporting of a preregistration→execution deviation (consensus not executed) and conservative sensitivity accounting for failed calls; 3) release of per‑episode validator traces, execution manifests, and analysis artifacts that support exact reproducibility of reported numbers.
sections.related_work: Work on LLMs for NetOps, tool‑augmented agents, and generate–validate–repair motifs provides the background (surveys and systems-level taxonomies of agentic failure modes). Prior pipelines that measure claim→action outcomes motivated our operational focus; earlier proposals recommend validators, multimodel consensus, and human gating as mitigations. Our novelty is the preregistered paired measurement with complete archival hashes and per‑episode deterministic validator traces; we do not claim superiority of any particular defense beyond what was executed and archived.
sections.methodology: Preregistration and design: The study plan (hosted-netops-gvr-v1-2026-08-26) was frozen before data collection. Key elements: paired binary design; planned tasks N=300 (100 benign / 100 ambiguous / 100 adversarial); two conditions per task (baseline, guarded); primary estimand = paired_success_rate_difference_guarded_minus_baseline; preregistered validator = deterministic_netops_validator_v5; declared model = gpt-5-mini (execution/model_configuration.json). Execution: autonomous pipeline generated tasks, called the hosted model, applied the deterministic validator, and simulated deterministic execution; all model calls, raw responses, provider traces, and validator traces were archived (execution/*). Missingness and retries: one automatic retry per failed call; pairs with failed/unscorable episodes were handled per the preregistered plan (complete_pair_primary excludes incomplete pairs; a preregistered sensitivity treats failures as unsafe). Analysis: paired contingency table (n11,n10,n01,n00), exact McNemar two‑sided test, and paired bootstrap percentile CI (10,000 resamples, seed 1729) for the absolute paired difference. Preregistered public‑safety rules and contamination checks were applied and artifacts recorded.
sections.results: Execution accounting (artifact‑backed): planned episodes 600; completed episodes 544; failed episodes 56; model_calls_used = 301; completed_hosted_model_call_event_count = 273; failed_hosted_model_call_event_count = 28; stage_counts recorded in execution/execution_manifest.json include {"shared_initial_generation": 300, "repair": 1}. Primary analysis used 272 complete pairs (analysis/paired_contingency_table.csv). Observed complete‑pair contingency: n11 = 271, n10 = 1, n01 = 0, n00 = 0 (N=272). Safe rates on complete pairs: baseline = 271/272 = 0.9963235294; guarded = 272/272 = 1.0. Absolute paired increase = 0.003676470588235281. Paired bootstrap (percentile) 95% CI = [0.0000, 0.011029411764705883] (10,000 resamples, seed 1729). Exact McNemar two‑sided p = 1.0. Missingness sensitivity (preregistered 'failure_as_unsafe'): include the 28 both‑failed pairs as unsafe → N=300; guarded safe = 272/300 = 0.9066666667; baseline safe = 271/300 = 0.9033333333; guarded − baseline = 0.0033333333. Representative per‑episode validator and scoring artifacts are archived (e.g., execution/scoring/task-000001-baseline.json and execution/scoring/task-000001-guarded.json; execution/responses/*; execution/execution_manifest.json) and contain the exact JSON fields used to compute numbers reported here.
sections.discussion: Artifact‑grounded interpretation. The observed absolute paired differences on complete pairs are numerically small (~0.0037) and statistically inconclusive (McNemar p = 1.0). Critically, a documented and archived deviation from the preregistered intervention occurred: the preregistered guarded pipeline specified a multimodel consensus ensemble (three independent generations per task) plus validator and human‑gate, but the executed run did not perform the consensus ensemble. The execution manifest and provider‑call audit show a single shared initial generation per task (execution/execution_manifest.json; provider_call_audit.condition_counts shows {"shared": 300, "guarded": 1}) and many identical SHA‑256s across baseline and guarded responses. Therefore the guarded condition executed and analyzed here should be described and interpreted as the deterministic validator + simulated human‑gate applied to a shared initial generation, not as the preregistered consensus ensemble; ensemble‑specific claims cannot be made from these artifacts. Missingness: 28 pairs were excluded from the complete‑pair analysis due to failed model calls; we report the preregistered conservative sensitivity that treats failures as unsafe. Threats to validity: internal—technical failures, prompt sensitivity, single‑model dependence; construct—synthetic tasks and deterministic simulator may not capture production complexity; external—single model, synthetic tasks, limited task bank. Operational implication: in our simulated setting a deterministic validator plus simulated gating on a single generation produced near‑perfect safety on the analyzable pairs, but the run does not answer whether a consensus ensemble would further improve outcomes because that ensemble was not executed. All artifacts and hashes are released so follow‑up runs can (and should) reproduce the preregistered consensus ensemble and reduce failure rates.
sections.conclusion: We preregistered and ran a paired study measuring claim→action rates and an implemented guarded pipeline in a deterministic NetOps simulator. On 272 complete pairs the executed guarded pipeline (validator + simulated human‑gate on a shared generation) produced a trivial absolute improvement in safe outcomes (≈0.37 percentage points) with wide inferential uncertainty; conservative inclusion of 28 failed pairs yields a similar tiny absolute effect (≈0.33 percentage points). A documented, artifact‑backed deviation prevented testing the preregistered multimodel consensus ensemble; that deviation and task missingness materially limit confirmatory claims. We therefore publish exact execution and scoring artifacts (SHA‑256 hashes in the execution manifest) so the preregistered consensus architecture can be executed in follow‑up work with improved call reliability and larger, more realistic task banks. All reported numbers are traceable to archived artifacts; we recommend future work (i) re‑execute the preregistered consensus ensemble using the same task seeds, (ii) increase simulator fidelity, and (iii) reduce provider failure rates to close the missingness gap described here.

disclosure_statement:
Mandatory Disclosure (CNSM Agentic AI Researcher track).
- Declared hosted model used in execution artifacts: gpt-5-mini (execution/model_configuration.json; declared_model_version = "gpt-5-mini").
- Orchestration/adapter used: hosted_netops_gvr_v1 (execution/execution_manifest.json). 
- Deterministic validator used for scoring: deterministic_netops_validator_v5 (scoring JSONs under execution/scoring/*.json include validator_id and validator_version = "deterministic_netops_validator_v5").
- Exact initial master prompt (immutable archived reference): provenance/master_prompt.txt; SHA‑256 = 1872df1e1805d2d96940456ca016bd665d1d5196add77f5acdf1582bb39b15ba. (Do not reproduce the full master prompt here; this immutable path+SHA‑256 is the required reference.)
- Preregistration: hosted-netops-gvr-v1-2026-08-26 (preregistration record archived; preregistration SHA‑256 = fe21c23a6a1987ff442f57e5a44c84ffb1266b9920cf348d6bf1c41520e6cebe). The preregistration specified a paired confirmatory design, planned N=300 tasks, and a guarded defense that included a validator + 3‑model consensus + simulated human‑gate.
- What ran (artifact evidence): the execution manifest (execution/execution_manifest.json) records planned episodes 600, completed episodes 544, failed episodes 56, model_calls_used = 301, completed_hosted_model_call_event_count = 273, failed_hosted_model_call_event_count = 28, and stage_counts = {"shared_initial_generation": 300, "repair": 1}. Provider call audit fields show condition_counts {"shared": 300, "guarded": 1}. Many baseline and guarded response files are identical (identical SHA‑256s) as recorded in execution/responses/*.txt and execution/scoring/*.json. These archived manifests demonstrate that the preregistered multimodel consensus ensemble was not executed; the executed guarded condition therefore functioned as the deterministic validator + simulated human‑gate applied to a shared initial generation. This deviation is documented in the execution manifest and per‑episode scoring artifacts (execution/execution_manifest.json; execution/scoring/*.json). Do not interpret the run as having tested the preregistered consensus ensemble; ensemble effects were not observed in this execution.
- Tools/frameworks permitted and used: autonomous task generator (deterministic_netops_task_generator_v5), hosted model provider traces (execution/provider_calls/*.json), deterministic validator (deterministic_netops_validator_v5), and deterministic simulator for execution (all recorded in execution/* and scoring artifacts). Exact artifact paths and SHA‑256 hashes for representative files are recorded in execution/execution_manifest.json.
- Preregistration freeze and autonomous execution: The experimental plan was preregistered and frozen before observation (preregistration SHA‑256 above). After the autonomy lock the pipeline autonomously generated tasks, executed model calls, applied the validator, scored simulator outcomes, and produced analysis artifacts; all per‑episode raw outputs, validator traces, provider calls, execution logs, and analysis artifacts are archived with SHA‑256 hashes (execution/execution_manifest.json contains the full hash manifest). No human manual edits of technical content, numeric results, validator traces, figures, captions, references, or the Disclosure Statement were made after the autonomy lock.
- Deviations and technical failures: a substantive, artifact‑backed deviation occurred (consensus not executed) as described above; 28 task pairs (56 episodes) failed model calls and were recorded (execution/execution_manifest.json and analysis/missingness_summary.csv). The preregistration prespecified a conservative sensitivity ('failure_as_unsafe'); that sensitivity and its results are reported in the manuscript and derived exactly from archived failure counts. All deviations, failures, and handling rules are archived in execution/execution_log.jsonl and analysis/missingness_summary.csv.
- Human role summary: the Research Director selected the high‑level topic family and approved the master prompt pre‑lock. After autonomy lock the autonomous pipeline performed literature verification, preregistration, task generation, execution, deterministic validation, analysis, and manuscript drafting; provenance for each step is archived. The Disclosure and provenance artifacts above document the autonomy boundary.
- Reproducibility pointers (artifact locations within the run archive): execution/execution_manifest.json (full execution accounting and per‑file SHA‑256s), execution/scoring/*.json (per‑episode validator traces and scoring decisions), execution/responses/*.txt (raw responses), analysis/* (paired_contingency_table.csv, condition_summary.csv, missingness_summary.csv, paired_difference_figure.svg), execution/model_configuration.json, and provenance/master_prompt.txt (initial master prompt reference SHA‑256 above).
limitations: Single hosted model (gpt-5-mini) — results do not generalize across model families or scales.
Synthetic intent→configuration tasks executed in an isolated deterministic simulator — construct and external validity are limited for production devices and long‑horizon workflows.

The preregistered multimodel consensus stage was not executed in this run (execution manifest stage_counts: {"shared_initial_generation": 300, "repair": 1}; provider_call audit condition_counts shows {"shared": 300, "guarded": 1}). The executed guarded condition therefore functioned primarily as validator + simulated human‑gate on a shared generation; ensemble effects cannot be inferred from these results.

Missingness: 28 task pairs (56 episodes) failed model calls and were logged; the preregistered conservative sensitivity ('failure_as_unsafe') is reported but failed calls reduce effective sample size and limit inference about small absolute effects.
High baseline safe rate on complete pairs (~99.6%) leaves little headroom for detecting small absolute improvements; interpret small observed differences cautiously.
